title: Activity snapshot bundles: time-sliced search & role-aware export presets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a first-class feature in the Console for creating time-sliced 'activity snapshot' bundles from the audit store that users can search, filter, save as presets, and export as role-aware CSV/NDJSON bundles. This ticket covers backend export orchestration and the Console UX for building, saving, and re-running snapshots with strict RBAC v2 enforcement and SSO/SAML-compatible access flows. Goal: let admins and auditors produce reproducible activity snapshots (e.g., last 24h failed logins + admin changes) with deterministic columns and redaction rules, while preventing data leakage and excessive load on the audit store.
acceptance_criteria: Console allows building time-sliced queries with filters: user, action, resource, time range, result, region, request_id
Users can save a query as a named preset (saved query) in the Console and re-run it with one click
Backend export job produces downloadable bundles in CSV and NDJSON; CSV columns are stable and documented
Export respects RBAC v2: only fields/rows permitted by the requesting principal are included; role-based redaction applied where needed
Large exports are performed as background bundle jobs; UI shows progress, partial preview, and issues warnings for >1M rows
Signed, time-limited URLs are issued for completed bundles; bundles auto-expire and are quarantined for compliance retention windows
Audit of the export action itself is recorded (who exported what preset, query, and time range)
Unit and integration tests cover: permission checks, redaction rules, CSV/NDJSON format correctness, and streaming correctness under concurrent requests
design_notes: Use 'time-sliced bundles' concept instead of streaming single cursor downloads: snapshot = consistent view of matching events at job start
Trade-off: snapshot consistency increases storage/compute for large windows but prevents non-determinism when running saved queries for audits
Prefer NDJSON for downstream ingestion and CSV for human review; implement shared schema mapper to guarantee parity between formats
RBAC enforcement should be enforced server-side at the event-serialization layer to avoid client-side holes
Signed download URLs must be short-lived and include preview tokens for first 100 rows to avoid repeatedly triggering exports
implementation_tasks: Backend: export orchestration service - accept query spec + principal, materialize snapshot, spawn workers to serialize partitions to storage
Backend: server-side event serializer with field-level redaction rules keyed to RBAC v2 policies and blame metadata
Backend: quota throttling + circuit breaker for concurrent export jobs per org to protect the audit store
API: new endpoints - POST /v1/audit/snapshots (create), GET /v1/audit/snapshots/:id/status, GET /v1/audit/snapshots/:id/download
Console: UX for saved presets - create/edit, description, last-run metadata, attachments to policy groups
Console: preview pane that streams first 100 rows quickly using limited read and enforced redaction
Console: job list / notifications and signed URL handling; surface retention and compliance labels
Integrations: ensure SSO/SAML role mappings are honored when evaluating RBAC v2 policies for export actors
Ops: add dashboards for export job latency, failure rates, and throttled job counts
Security: request a formal security review and threat model for export leakage and signed URL abuse
qa_plan: Manual: run saved presets across admin/non-admin roles to validate row/field redaction
Manual: export large (simulated) datasets to validate background job scaling and signed URL expiration
Automated: end-to-end tests that create snapshot, wait for completion, download CSV/NDJSON, validate schema and sample rows
Load: synthetic concurrent-export test to validate quota enforcement and circuit breakers
Compliance: verify retention/quarantine logic matches retention policies and that exported bundles are logged with export metadata
